name: Troll, Ice (Mythic)
body:
MYTHIC ICE TROLL
CR 5/MR 2

This large creature has light blue-green skin and cold, piercing eyes. Dressed in rough furs, its features are sharp with jagged icicles dangling from its frozen flesh.

XP 1,600
CE Large humanoid (cold, giant, mythic)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 13, flat-footed 15 (+4 Dex, +6 natural, –1 size)
hp 61 (6d8+34); regeneration 5 (acid or fire)
Fort +8, Ref +8, Will +2
DR 5/epic; Immune cold
Weaknesses slashing susceptibility, vulnerable to fire

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee rime shard spear +8 (2d6+7/x3 plus 1d6 cold) and bite +3 (1d6+2) or bite +8 (1d6+5) and 2 claws +8 (1d4+5)
Ranged rime shard dart +7 (1d6+4 plus 1d6 cold)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks feral savagery (rend), mythic power (2/day, surge +1d6), rend (2 claws, 1d6+7 plus freezing blood), rime shard

STATISTICS

Str 21, Dex 18, Con 16, Int 9, Wis 10, Cha 7
Base Atk +4; CMB +10; CMD 24
Feats Intimidating Prowess, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Perception)
Skills Intimidate +8, Perception +9, Survival +4
Languages Giant
SQ freezing blood

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Freezing Blood (Su)

When a mythic ice troll takes piercing or slashing damage, the attacker (or another creature adjacent to the troll, if the attacker is not adjacent to it) is sprayed with the troll’s super-chilled blood. This deals 1d4 cold damage (DC 16 Fortitude half ), and if the creature fails the save it also takes 1d4 nonlethal damage and is fatigued from hypothermia until the nonlethal damage is removed.

When the troll uses its rend attack, it freezes the target’s blood instead. The target takes 1d4 bleed damage, and each time they take that bleed damage they must save as if exposed to the troll’s blood.

Rime Shard (Ex)

The troll can snap off the icicles covering its frozen flesh, extending them into sharp spears to wield in melee.

They also can hurl these shards like darts, and a living creature struck by a hurled shard is coated in ice, affecting them as a tanglefoot bag, though each round a creature ends its turn entangled by a rime shard, it takes another 1d4 cold damage.

The entangling ice can be shattered with bludgeoning, piercing, fire, or sonic damage.

The troll can expend one use of its mythic power as a full-round action to make one rime shard attack against each creature in a 15-foot cone adjacent to itself or a 10-foot square anywhere within 20 feet. In addition to the attack, the area is scattered with icicles equivalent to a spike stones spell lasting 1 minute, dealing an additional 1d4 points of cold damage for each 5 feet.

Slashing Susceptibility (Ex)

If the troll takes at least 10 points of slashing damage from a single attack, one of its arms is severed (DC 14 Fortitude negates). The severed limb can move independently (speed 15 feet) and can fight as if still attached; treat its attacks and attacks against it as if it were prone. A severed arm has 15 hit points, which are separate from the troll’s own hit points, and it regenerates independently as well. Killing the arm does not harm the troll’s body and vice versa. The troll can pick up a severed arm as a move action and it reattaches itself at the end of the troll’s turn.

If the troll takes a critical hit from a slashing weapon, as an immediate action it can choose to take normal damage from the attack instead but automatically have an arm severed.

If both of a troll’s arms are severed, it can instead choose to have one of its legs severed. Treat a troll missing one leg as entangled.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold mountains or underground
Organization solitary or band (1 mythic ice troll and 3–6 ice trolls)
Treasure standard

A severed leg can’t attack but can make trip or bull rush combat maneuvers. If it loses both legs, the body falls prone. It may instead to have its head severed. Its head can act independently, making bite attacks. Its headless body is treated as blind.

Ice trolls are somewhat smaller than normal trolls, but they possess greater intelligence and cunning and are just as voraciously hungry. They display the typical hunched posture of trolls, combined with long arms tipped with sharp claws, though their underbite is less pronounced.

They may wield forged weapons but can make deadly piercing weapons from their own icy flesh, though they are equally adept with savage rending claws. An ice troll stands about 10 feet tall and weighs up to 900 pounds.

Ice trolls enjoy the taste of human flesh, and those not working with humans frequently set traps near civilized areas to catch their favorite prey. They will also raid isolated settlements for food, often bringing captured humans back to their icy lairs, where the unfortunate victims are caged and fattened up before finally being devoured by the voracious trolls. They fight more cautiously and cleverly than normal trolls, focusing on the weakest enemies or those bearing fire to bring them down.

Ice troll society is more patriarchal than normal troll society, and while males may form gangs to hunt or raid, most ice trolls live in small family groups comprised of a male, a female, and their offspring.
